title: Space Stoichiometry
description: Calculate ore needed for fuel through a chain of chemical reactions, then maximize fuel from 1 trillion ore.
writeup:
## Approach

Work backwards from FUEL to ORE, tracking surpluses from batch production. Then binary search for Part 2.

## Part 1

Start with a demand for 1 FUEL. For each non-ORE chemical still needed, look up its recipe, compute how many batches are required (`ceil(needed / batch_size)`), track any surplus, and add the input requirements. Repeat until only ORE demands remain. Surpluses matter because reactions produce in fixed batch sizes — e.g., needing 7 of something produced in batches of 10 leaves 3 surplus for later use.

## Part 2

The `ore_for_fuel(n)` function is monotonically increasing, so binary search works. Start with a lower bound of `1T / ore_per_fuel` (assuming perfect efficiency) and double it for the upper bound. Binary search converges in ~30 steps to find the maximum fuel producible from exactly 1 trillion ore.
